about: ENCORE. Audio Processing's reference set: inputs (recipes for dsp/ReferenceSignals.h) and the results every build must give, each within its tolerance. Written by tools/reference.py; checked by tests/ReferenceTests.cpp and wasm/reference.mjs.

exact.why: Integer results (counts, lengths, notes, sample frames, kit maps) and sample peaks of the generated inputs: the same on every system.

lufs.why: Loudness, LUFS: double-precision filters and sums; systems differ in float rounding and the maths library's log10 and pow.

lu.why: Loudness range, LU: a difference of two percentiles of short-term loudness, each within the lufs allowance.

db.why: Levels in dB (peaks, RMS, balance): log10 of a float, rounding and the maths library.

peak.why: True peak, linear: the 4x upsampler's sums in float, which compilers order and fuse differently (MSVC /fp:fast, FMA on arm64); 1e-5 is 0.0001 dB.

hz.why: A detected pitch, Hz: YIN's sums of differences and the interpolated dip, which compilers order and fuse differently; 1e-5 is 0.017 cents.

cents.why: Cents from the nearest note: the hz allowance through log2.

clarity.why: How periodic a voice is, 0 to 1: the depth of YIN's dip, rounding only.

bpm.why: Tempo, BPM: the best of a fixed grid of tempos, scored on an onset envelope made by an FFT (Accelerate on Apple systems), so only a near tie between two grid tempos could move it.

frames.why: An onset's position, sample frames: found to a fraction of a sample by a fitted predictor; rounding moves the fraction slightly.

master-lufs.why: A master's loudness, LUFS: the whole chain (learning, oversampled saturation and limiting) runs in float over tens of seconds of audio, so rounding adds up; still a tenth of the 0.1 LU the driver aims within.

master-db.why: What mastering learned (gains, dB): the same long float chain as master-lufs.

master-peak.why: The master's true peak, linear: the same long float chain as master-lufs (0.002 is 0.02 dB).

sound-length.why: A sound's length in samples is the floor of the sample rate times a length in seconds; compilers that reorder arithmetic (MSVC /fp:fast, which the products build with) can round that product across a whole number, adding or losing one sample of the tail.

sound-sum.why: A sound's sum of |x|: synthesized with sin and exp, which maths libraries round differently in the last place, and one sample more or less of a tail (see sound-length).

sound-peak.why: A sound's peak: rounding in sin and exp only (a tail sample is never the peak).

seconds.why: A time in seconds worked out from sample positions: rounding in the division only.

ratio.why: A correlation or share between -1 and 1: sums of products in double, ordered differently by compilers.

level.why: A linear level (DC offset, RMS, a difference, a waveform column): float or double sums, rounding only.

spectrum.why: Spectrum values and their sums: a float FFT (Accelerate on Apple systems), windowing and smoothing; rounding differs by system.

spectrum-db.why: Levels in dB read from averaged spectra (tonal balance, a learned body curve): the spectrum allowance through log10.

music-math.why: Hz and MIDI conversions in double: log2 and pow from the maths library, last-place differences only.

proc-sum.why: A processed signal's sum of |x|: filters, envelopes, oversampling and pitch shifting in float, which compilers order and fuse differently, over seconds of audio; 1e-3 is 0.009 dB, far below any audible or setting change.

proc-peak.why: A processed signal's peak: as proc-sum.

proc-lufs.why: A processed signal's integrated loudness, LUFS: as proc-sum.
